catalog_note: All scenarios assume German employment law. Always check for collective agreements (Tarifverträge) that may provide greater employee protections than statutory minimums.

hr_scenarios.name: Dismissal During Probation Period (Probezeit)
hr_scenarios.description: Employer wishes to dismiss an employee who is still within the agreed probationary period (maximum 6 months under § 622 Abs. 3 BGB).
hr_scenarios.kschg_note: KSchG does not apply during the first 6 months of employment — the employee has no unfair dismissal protection. However, general protections (AGG, MuSchG, BetrVG) still apply.

notice_period.notes: 2 weeks notice during probation. Check contract and any applicable Tarifvertrag for longer periods.

hr_scenarios.works_council_note: Even during probation, Works Council must be consulted under § 102 BetrVG before the dismissal is issued. Failure renders the dismissal void.
escalation_triggers: Employee is pregnant or has notified pregnancy within the last 2 weeks
Employee is on or has applied for parental leave (Elternzeit)
Employee has a recognized severe disability (GdB ≥ 50) or pending application
Employee is a Works Council member
Employee has filed a complaint (e.g., discrimination, whistleblower) in the last 6 months
Dismissal reason could be seen as relating to a protected characteristic (§ 1 AGG)
required_steps: 1. Confirm the probation period: check the employment contract for start date and agreed probation length (max 6 months)
2. Run the protected employee check (pregnancy, Elternzeit, severe disability, Works Council membership)
3. If any protection applies: STOP — escalate to Legal before proceeding
4. Prepare the Works Council consultation notice (§ 102 BetrVG): name, employment date, position, reason for dismissal, notice period
5. Submit the consultation notice to the Works Council — they have 1 week to respond for an ordinary dismissal
6. Wait for the Works Council response or expiry of the 1-week window before issuing the dismissal letter
7. Issue the written dismissal letter (Kündigungsschreiben) — must be signed in wet ink (§ 623 BGB), no email
8. Arrange personal handover of the letter or send by registered post with acknowledgment of receipt
9. Document everything: consultation notice, Works Council response (or non-response), delivery confirmation
10. Update the employee record in HR system

hr_authority.conditions: Only if no protected employee status applies and Works Council consultation is completed

common_mistakes: Issuing the dismissal before the Works Council consultation window has expired
Sending the dismissal letter by email (legally void under § 623 BGB)
Forgetting to check for pregnancy — an employee who notified pregnancy AFTER the dismissal letter was prepared but BEFORE it was handed over is still protected
Assuming no Works Council exists — verify this; a Works Council can be formed at any time

hr_scenarios.name: Ordinary Conduct Dismissal (Verhaltensbedingte Kündigung)
hr_scenarios.description: Employer wishes to dismiss an employee for conduct reasons (e.g., repeated tardiness, insubordination, policy violations, verbal misconduct). KSchG applies.
hr_scenarios.kschg_note: For conduct dismissal to be socially justified under KSchG, a prior written warning (Abmahnung) is almost always required unless the conduct is so serious that the employee could not reasonably have expected to keep their job (e.g., theft, fraud).

notice_period.notes: Minimum 4 weeks to the 15th or end of month. Increases with tenure — see notice period table in legal-escalation-and-compliance.md.

hr_scenarios.works_council_note: § 102 BetrVG: Works Council must be fully informed and consulted before issuing any dismissal. Insufficient consultation information renders the dismissal void.
hr_scenarios.prerequisite: At least one written warning (Abmahnung) for the same or closely related type of conduct must have been issued and documented, unless the conduct makes continuation of employment unreasonable.
escalation_triggers: No prior written warning has been issued for this type of conduct
The incident that triggered the dismissal is more than 2 years old
Employee is in a protected category (pregnancy, Elternzeit, severe disability, BetrVG mandate)
Employee has filed a grievance, discrimination complaint, or whistleblower report in the last 12 months
The conduct involves potential criminal activity (theft, fraud, assault) — extraordinary dismissal may be more appropriate
Employee is subject to a collective agreement with stricter dismissal requirements
Company has fewer than 11 full-time equivalent employees — KSchG may not apply, but caution still required
required_steps: 1. Confirm KSchG applies: employee has been employed for more than 6 months AND the company employs more than 10 full-time equivalent employees
2. Run the protected employee check
3. If any protection applies: STOP — escalate to Legal
4. Verify that at least one written Abmahnung has been issued for the same or related conduct — locate it in the employee file
5. If no Abmahnung exists and the conduct is not severe enough to skip the warning step: issue an Abmahnung first and allow a reasonable period before considering dismissal
6. Assess whether the conduct is sufficiently serious and recent to justify dismissal (documented incidents from last 12–24 months)
7. Prepare the full Works Council consultation package: name, date of employment, dismissal type (ordinary/conduct), notice period, summary of incidents, and copies of prior warnings
8. Submit to Works Council — they have 1 week to respond for ordinary dismissal
9. After Works Council response or expiry of window: issue the written dismissal letter with correct notice period
10. Hand-deliver or send by registered post — do not email
11. Document the full process in the employee file

hr_authority.conditions: Conduct dismissals under KSchG carry significant litigation risk — Legal should review the case before the dismissal is issued
hr_authority.requires_legal_if: KSchG applies — Legal review recommended in all cases

common_mistakes: Skipping the Abmahnung step and going straight to dismissal
Writing an Abmahnung that is too vague ('attitude problems') rather than describing specific behavior
Providing incomplete information to the Works Council — they must receive all facts that the employer is relying on
Using incidents in the dismissal letter that were not included in the Works Council consultation (those incidents cannot be relied upon)
Dismissing during or shortly after a protected leave — creates appearance of retaliation

hr_scenarios.name: Ordinary Performance Dismissal (Personenbedingte Kündigung)
hr_scenarios.description: Employer wishes to dismiss an employee due to persistent underperformance, incapacity, or long-term illness. Distinct from conduct dismissal — no fault or warning required, but the bar is high.
hr_scenarios.kschg_note: Performance/person-based dismissal must be proportionate. Employer must show: (1) the performance deficit is persistent and unlikely to improve, (2) less severe measures (retraining, role change) have been considered or tried, (3) the business impact is concrete.

notice_period.notes: Same as conduct — increases with tenure.

escalation_triggers: Employee has been on sick leave for more than 6 weeks in the last 12 months — long-term illness dismissal has additional hurdles (betriebliches Eingliederungsmanagement / BEM required)
Employee has a disability or chronic illness that may be causing the underperformance — dismissal may conflict with SGB IX and AGG
No documented performance management process has taken place (no targets set, no feedback given, no support offered)
Employee is in a protected category
Employer has not offered a BEM (Betriebliches Eingliederungsmanagement) where sick leave exceeded 6 weeks in 12 months
required_steps: 1. Confirm KSchG applies
2. Run the protected employee check

3. Check sick leave record: if employee has been off more than 6 consecutive weeks OR more than 6 weeks cumulative in the last 12 months, a BEM (§ 167 Abs. 2 SGB IX) must have been offered — if not, proceed to BEM before dismissal
4. Review the documented performance management history: targets set, reviews held, feedback given, support offered
5. If no adequate performance management process: do not proceed to dismissal yet — implement PIP or performance review process first
6. Assess whether alternative placement in a different role is possible
7. Prepare the Works Council consultation package including full performance history
8. Submit to Works Council — 1 week response window
9. Issue written dismissal with correct notice period after Works Council window
10. Document all steps in the employee file

hr_authority.requires_legal_if: Always — performance dismissals are heavily litigated in German employment courts

common_mistakes: Issuing a performance dismissal without any prior performance management process
Forgetting the BEM requirement for employees with significant sick leave history
Conflating performance issues with conduct issues — choose the right dismissal type
Not exploring role transfers or reasonable adjustments before dismissal

hr_scenarios.name: Extraordinary / Immediate Dismissal (Außerordentliche Kündigung fristlos)
hr_scenarios.description: Employer dismisses an employee with immediate effect for serious cause — no notice period. Typically used for theft, fraud, serious assault, deliberate sabotage, serious breach of confidentiality.
hr_scenarios.kschg_note: The bar for extraordinary dismissal is very high. The conduct must be so serious that continuing the employment relationship — even for the notice period — is unreasonable. Courts scrutinize these closely.

notice_period.notes: No notice period. However, a social compensation payment (Abfindung) is sometimes agreed in settlement even for extraordinary dismissals.

hard_deadline.description: § 626 Abs. 2 BGB: The extraordinary dismissal must be issued within 2 weeks of the employer becoming aware of the facts justifying it. This deadline is absolute — missing it makes the extraordinary dismissal void.
hard_deadline.clock_starts: Date the authorized HR/management decision-maker first learned of the facts

hr_scenarios.works_council_note: Works Council consultation for extraordinary dismissal: only 3 days (not 1 week). This is because of the 2-week overall deadline. The consultation package must be submitted immediately.
hr_scenarios.protected_employee_note: Even for extraordinary dismissal, special protections apply. For pregnant employees and Works Council members, an extraordinary dismissal requires specific additional steps (Works Council consent for Works Council members; state authority approval for pregnant employees).
escalation_triggers: Any protected employee category — immediate Legal escalation
The employee is a Works Council member — extraordinary dismissal requires Works Council consent (§ 103 BetrVG) or labor court authorization
Criminal conduct is involved — coordinate with legal and potentially law enforcement
The 2-week deadline is at risk of being missed
The facts are disputed or unclear — do not issue until facts are established
required_steps: 1. Establish and document the exact date the relevant decision-maker first learned of the incident — the 2-week clock starts here
2. Assess whether the facts are sufficiently clear and serious to justify immediate dismissal
3. Run the protected employee check — CRITICAL for this dismissal type
4. If employee is a Works Council member: STOP — Works Council consent under § 103 BetrVG required first, or labor court authorization needed — escalate to Legal immediately
5. Consider whether to suspend the employee pending investigation (paid garden leave) while facts are established — do this before the 2-week clock runs out
6. Prepare the Works Council consultation package: full facts, date of incident, reason for extraordinary dismissal — submit immediately (3-day response window)
7. After Works Council response or expiry of 3-day window: issue the extraordinary dismissal letter
8. Ensure the letter is delivered within the 2-week deadline from awareness date
9. Hand-deliver if at all possible — get signed acknowledgment
10. Document timeline meticulously — courts will scrutinize every date

hr_authority.requires_legal_if: Always — extraordinary dismissal is the highest-risk employment action. Legal must be involved from the moment the facts are known.

common_mistakes: Missing the 2-week § 626 deadline — this is the single most common reason extraordinary dismissals fail in court
Not consulting the Works Council in time due to the compressed 3-day window
Issuing an extraordinary dismissal without sufficient evidence — 'we think he did it' is not enough
Forgetting that a Works Council member cannot be extraordinarily dismissed without the Works Council's consent or a court order

hr_scenarios.name: Operational Redundancy (Betriebsbedingte Kündigung)
hr_scenarios.description: Employee's role is eliminated due to operational, structural, or economic reasons. The decision is business-driven, not employee-driven.
hr_scenarios.kschg_note: Operational redundancy must be socially justified. The employer must: (1) have a genuine operational reason, (2) perform a Sozialauswahl (social selection) among comparable employees, (3) check for alternative placement. Sozialauswahl criteria: length of service, age, maintenance obligations, severe disability.

notice_period.notes: Increases with tenure. Redundancy packages (Abfindung) are common in practice but not legally required unless agreed.

hr_scenarios.works_council_note: For individual redundancies: standard § 102 BetrVG consultation. For collective redundancies (≥5 employees in companies of 21–59 employees, or ≥10% in larger companies): § 17 KSchG notification to the Agentur für Arbeit AND potential Interessenausgleich/Sozialplan obligation with the Works Council.
sozialauswahl_criteria: Maintenance obligations (Unterhaltspflichten) — dependent children, non-working spouse
escalation_triggers: Any protected employee is included in or affected by the redundancy pool
More than 5 employees are being made redundant — collective redundancy rules may apply
The operational reason is not clearly documented or may not withstand scrutiny
The Sozialauswahl has not been formally conducted
Employee's role has been or will soon be refilled — undermines the operational reason claim
Company has a Works Council and no Interessenausgleich discussion has been initiated
required_steps: 1. Confirm and document the operational reason: restructuring decision, cost reduction, technology replacement — decision must be made and documented before the dismissal
2. Define the comparable employee pool for Sozialauswahl (same or similar roles, interchangeability)
3. Apply the four Sozialauswahl criteria to all employees in the pool — document scores
4. Identify which employee(s) have the lowest social protection score and therefore can be dismissed
5. Check whether any of the selected employees are in a protected category
6. Check whether the role can be filled by the employee elsewhere in the company (alternative placement obligation)
7. Check whether mass redundancy thresholds are met — if yes, escalate to Legal immediately
8. Prepare Works Council consultation package including the Sozialauswahl documentation
9. For larger restructurings: initiate Interessenausgleich negotiations with the Works Council
10. Issue dismissal letters with correct notice periods after Works Council process
11. File notification with Agentur für Arbeit if mass redundancy thresholds are met

hr_authority.requires_legal_if: Always for redundancies — Sozialauswahl errors are the most common basis for successful wrongful dismissal claims

common_mistakes: Selecting who to make redundant before conducting a formal Sozialauswahl
Refilling the role within 12 months — this makes the operational reason appear pretextual
Forgetting to check for comparable roles elsewhere in the company
Missing the mass redundancy notification obligation to the Agentur für Arbeit

hr_scenarios.name: Issuing a Written Warning (Abmahnung)
hr_scenarios.description: HR issues a formal written warning to an employee for misconduct or poor performance, as a prerequisite to a subsequent conduct or performance dismissal.
legal_basis: § 314 BGB (Abmahnung principle derived from case law)
hr_scenarios.kschg_note: An Abmahnung itself is not a dismissal, so KSchG does not directly apply. However, it becomes the evidentiary foundation for a later KSchG-governed dismissal.

notice_period.notes: An Abmahnung does not carry a notice period — it is a warning, not a dismissal.

hr_scenarios.works_council_note: No Works Council consultation required before issuing an Abmahnung. However, the employee has the right to attach a written response to their personnel file.
hr_scenarios.works_council_note_for_protected: For Works Council members, issuing an Abmahnung for activities within their Works Council role is prohibited.
escalation_triggers: The employee is a Works Council member and the Abmahnung relates to activities connected to their Works Council role
The conduct being warned about could be basis for an immediate extraordinary dismissal — consider whether Abmahnung or termination is the right response
The employee has already received 2+ Abmahnungen for similar conduct — consider whether dismissal is now appropriate
required_steps: 1. Identify the specific conduct or performance issue to be warned about
2. Verify that the incident is sufficiently recent (stale incidents lose their warning effect over time — typically 2–3 years)
3. Draft the Abmahnung with all required elements (see template in employment-law-playbooks.md)
4. Have the Abmahnung reviewed by HR management before issuing
5. Issue to the employee in writing — obtain written acknowledgment of receipt
6. Inform the employee they have the right to respond in writing and have their response attached to their personnel file
7. File the signed Abmahnung in the employee's personnel file
8. Set a calendar reminder: if no repeat conduct within 12–24 months, the Abmahnung loses some of its weight for subsequent dismissal — reassess
abmahnung_required_elements: Full name and position of the employee
Specific description of the conduct (what happened, when, where, who witnessed it) — must be precise, not generic
Statement that the conduct violates the employment contract or company policy (cite specific obligation)
Clear instruction to desist from this conduct in future
Warning that repetition may result in dismissal (Kündigung) without further warning
Date and signature of authorized HR representative

hr_authority.conditions: HR can issue Abmahnungen independently. Escalate to Legal if the employee is a Works Council member or if the conduct is serious enough to consider immediate dismissal instead.

common_mistakes: Vague language: 'your attitude needs to improve' — an Abmahnung must describe a specific incident
Not warning of the dismissal consequence — without the warning, the Abmahnung cannot support a later dismissal
Issuing an Abmahnung for a Works Council member's Works Council activities
Forgetting to give the employee the right to respond in writing

hr_scenarios.name: Fixed-Term Contract (Befristeter Arbeitsvertrag)
hr_scenarios.description: Employer wishes to hire an employee on a time-limited contract, or extend an existing fixed-term contract.

notice_period.notes: A fixed-term contract ends automatically on the agreed end date — no notice of dismissal required. However, if the employee is dismissed before the end date, normal dismissal rules apply.

hr_scenarios.works_council_note: Hiring decisions, including fixed-term hires, require Works Council involvement under § 99 BetrVG in companies with 20+ employees (Zustimmung zur Einstellung).

rules: Prohibited if the employee has previously worked for the same employer in any capacity (Vorbeschäftigungsverbot) — this applies for life per BAG 2011 ruling (with some caveats after BVerfG 2018)
Each extension must be agreed in writing before the current term expires — a late signature converts the contract to permanent employment
No maximum duration — as long as the objective reason exists
Objective reasons (§ 14 Abs. 1 TzBfG): temporary business need, replacing an absent employee, trial period, employee-requested, funding contingency, court settlement, nature of the work
The objective reason must genuinely exist and be documented at the time the contract is signed
If the objective reason is found to be pretextual, the contract becomes permanent

escalation_triggers: Employee has previously worked for TechForward in any capacity — prior employment check required before sachgrundlose Befristung
The contract is approaching or would exceed the 2-year maximum for sachgrundlose Befristung
A third extension is being proposed — this is the maximum; any further extension requires a Sachgrund or the contract becomes permanent
The Sachgrund being cited may not be legally sufficient — Legal to review
The extension agreement was not signed before the current term expired
required_steps: 1. Decide whether there is an objective reason (Sachgrund) or whether sachgrundlose Befristung will be used
2. If sachgrundlose: check prior employment history with TechForward — any prior employment in any role blocks sachgrundlose Befristung
3. Calculate total fixed-term duration — ensure it does not exceed 2 years for sachgrundlose
4. Count the number of extensions proposed — ensure they do not exceed 3 for sachgrundlose
5. Draft the contract or extension agreement in writing (§ 14 Abs. 4 TzBfG: must be in writing before employment begins, or before the extension takes effect)
6. If company has 20+ employees: submit to Works Council for Zustimmung under § 99 BetrVG
7. Both parties sign before the start date / extension effective date
8. Set a calendar reminder 3 months before the contract end date to decide: extend, convert to permanent, or allow to lapse

hr_authority.conditions: Standard sachgrundlose Befristung within limits. Escalate to Legal for Sachgrundbefristung or any edge cases.

common_mistakes: Signing the extension agreement after the current term has expired — the contract becomes permanent immediately upon expiry without a timely written extension
Using sachgrundlose Befristung for an employee who previously worked at TechForward
Exceeding 2 years total or 3 extensions under sachgrundlose Befristung
Not getting Works Council consent for new hires in companies with 20+ employees

hr_scenarios.name: Dismissal of a Severely Disabled Employee (Schwerbehinderter Arbeitnehmer)
hr_scenarios.description: Employer wishes to dismiss an employee with a recognized severe disability (Grad der Behinderung ≥ 50, or ≥ 30 with equal treatment status).
hr_scenarios.special_protection: Integrationsamt (now: Inklusionsamt) approval required before any dismissal. This is a mandatory precondition — the dismissal is void without it.

integrationsamt_process.approval_generally_granted_for: Operational redundancy, incapacity unrelated to disability
integrationsamt_process.approval_generally_refused_for: Dismissal where the reason is related to the disability, dismissal during BEM process

escalation_triggers: Always — this scenario must always involve Legal
Employee's disability status is pending recognition (GdB application in progress) — protection may still apply
The dismissal reason is related to illness or performance that may be connected to the disability
BEM (Betriebliches Eingliederungsmanagement) has not been offered or completed
required_steps: 1. Confirm disability status: check for Schwerbehindertenausweis or pending GdB application — protection applies if employer knows or should know of the disability
2. STOP — escalate to Legal immediately
3. Legal will apply to the Integrationsamt for approval (must happen before Works Council consultation for the dismissal can proceed)
4. Await Integrationsamt decision — typically 4–6 weeks
5. If approved: Legal prepares Works Council consultation package
6. Works Council consultation (1 week ordinary / 3 days extraordinary)
7. Issue dismissal only after both Integrationsamt approval and Works Council process are complete

hr_authority.requires_legal_if: Always — do not take any action without Legal involvement

common_mistakes: Proceeding with dismissal without Integrationsamt approval — the dismissal is automatically void
Not realizing that protection applies when a GdB application is pending and the employer is aware of the disability
Dismissing an employee for reasons related to their disability — this is both a KSchG violation and an AGG violation

hr_scenarios.name: Dismissal During Pregnancy or Maternity Protection (Schwangerschaft / Mutterschutz)
hr_scenarios.description: Employer becomes aware that an employee is pregnant or is within 4 months of giving birth and wishes to proceed with or maintain a dismissal.
hr_scenarios.special_protection: Absolute dismissal prohibition from the start of pregnancy until 4 months after birth (§ 17 MuSchG). Employer cannot dismiss — period. The only exception is approval by the state authority (Aufsichtsbehörde / Landesamt für Arbeitsschutz) for exceptional circumstances entirely unrelated to the pregnancy.
hr_scenarios.works_council_note: No Works Council consultation can substitute for Aufsichtsbehörde approval. Even with Works Council approval, the dismissal is void without state authority approval.
escalation_triggers: Always — the moment pregnancy becomes known, any pending dismissal must be stopped and Legal consulted

Employee notifies pregnancy AFTER a dismissal has been issued but BEFORE it takes legal effect — protection is retroactive (§ 17 Abs. 1 S. 2 MuSchG) if the employee notifies within 2 weeks of receiving the dismissal
required_steps: 1. STOP immediately — do not issue or proceed with any dismissal
2. Escalate to Legal immediately
3. If a dismissal has already been issued: check whether the employee notified pregnancy within 2 weeks — if so, the dismissal is void and must be withdrawn
4. Legal will assess whether the circumstances meet the narrow exception requiring state authority approval
5. If dismissal is still intended: Legal applies to the Aufsichtsbehörde — this is a high bar
6. Document all steps carefully — do not allow informal communication suggesting dismissal intent
common_mistakes: Proceeding with a dismissal that was planned before pregnancy was disclosed — protection applies retroactively if employee notifies within 2 weeks
Assuming the employee must have known about the pregnancy and chosen not to disclose — the protection period can extend back to conception

hr_scenarios.name: Dismissal During or After Parental Leave (Elternzeit)
hr_scenarios.description: Employer wishes to dismiss an employee who is currently on Elternzeit or has recently returned from parental leave.
hr_scenarios.special_protection: Dismissal prohibition applies from the date the employee applies for Elternzeit until its end (§ 18 BEEG). Exception: state authority (zuständige Behörde — typically Gewerbeaufsicht or Landesamt) must approve in extraordinary circumstances.
hr_scenarios.works_council_note: State authority approval is a prerequisite — Works Council consultation cannot substitute.
escalation_triggers: Any employee currently on or having applied for Elternzeit
Redundancy affects an employee on Elternzeit — Sozialauswahl must treat them as if still at work
required_steps: 1. STOP — escalate to Legal immediately
2. Legal assesses whether an extraordinary circumstance justifies applying to the state authority
3. If proceeding: Legal applies for state authority approval
4. Do not issue dismissal without approval
common_mistakes: Including an employee on Elternzeit in a redundancy without state authority approval
Failing to check whether Elternzeit has been applied for (application, not commencement, triggers protection)

hr_scenarios.name: Works Council Consultation (§ 102 BetrVG) — Standalone Process
hr_scenarios.description: Step-by-step guide to the Works Council consultation process required before any dismissal.
hr_scenarios.kschg_note: § 102 BetrVG applies regardless of whether KSchG applies. Even for employees with no unfair dismissal protection, Works Council must be consulted.

consultation_windows.note: The window starts when the Works Council receives the full consultation package, not when the dismissal is intended. If the Works Council raises objections, they must state reasons — the dismissal can still proceed but the employee gains additional rights.

works_council_responses.effect: Employer may proceed but must attach Works Council's concerns to the dismissal letter
Employer may still proceed BUT the employee gains the right to continue working (Weiterbeschäftigungsanspruch) pending any Arbeitsgericht proceedings

required_consultation_content: Employee's full name and date of birth
Intended date of dismissal / notice period end date
Dismissal reason — all facts the employer intends to rely on must be disclosed; facts not disclosed cannot be used in court
For redundancy: Sozialauswahl process and result
Whether the employee is subject to special protection (and if so, how it has been addressed)
void_conditions: Dismissal issued before the consultation window has expired
Works Council received incomplete or inaccurate information
No Works Council exists but one should — verify (threshold: ≥ 5 permanent employees)

hr_authority.conditions: HR can manage the § 102 process. Legal should review the consultation package for conduct and performance dismissals.

hr_scenarios.name: AGG-Compliant Hiring Process
hr_scenarios.description: HR is running a recruitment process and needs to ensure it complies with the Allgemeines Gleichbehandlungsgesetz (AGG) to avoid discrimination claims.
hr_scenarios.works_council_note: In companies with 20+ employees, Works Council co-determination right under § 99 BetrVG applies to all hires.
escalation_triggers: A rejected candidate explicitly references a protected characteristic or uses the word 'discrimination'
A job posting uses language that excludes a protected group
A hiring manager gives a rejection reason that references a protected characteristic
A candidate requests to see the documents related to the hiring decision within 2 months of the rejection
required_steps: 1. Review job posting for AGG-compliant language (no age preferences, gender-neutral, no discriminatory requirements)
2. Ensure all interviewers are briefed: questions about pregnancy, family planning, religion, disability are prohibited
3. Document the selection criteria before reviewing applications — objective criteria only
4. Document rejection reasons in writing using only objective, role-related criteria
5. Retain recruitment documentation for 2 months after rejection notification (AGG § 15 Abs. 4 limitation period)
6. If a candidate alleges discrimination: escalate to Legal immediately — AGG § 22 reverses the burden of proof if the candidate can demonstrate prima facie evidence of discrimination
7. Works Council consent under § 99 BetrVG before the candidate starts

hr_authority.conditions: Standard recruitment. Escalate if discrimination claim is made.

prohibited_interview_questions: Are you pregnant or planning to become pregnant?
Do you have children or plan to have children?
Do you have any disabilities or chronic illnesses?
How old are you? (where not relevant to the role)
What is your nationality or country of origin?
What is your sexual orientation or gender identity?

hr_scenarios.name: Betriebliches Eingliederungsmanagement (BEM)
hr_scenarios.description: An employee has been unable to work for more than 6 weeks in the last 12 months. The employer must offer BEM (occupational integration management) before any illness-related dismissal.
hr_scenarios.kschg_note: BEM is not a dismissal scenario — it is a mandatory preventive process. However, failure to offer BEM significantly weakens any subsequent illness-related dismissal in court.
hr_scenarios.works_council_note: Works Council must be involved in the BEM process if the employee consents (§ 167 Abs. 2 S. 5 SGB IX).
hr_scenarios.trigger: Employee has been unable to work (sick) for more than 6 weeks cumulatively in the last 12 months (not necessarily consecutive).
required_steps: 1. Monitor sick leave records — flag when any employee reaches 6 weeks in 12 months
2. Send a written BEM invitation to the employee — explain what BEM is, that participation is voluntary, and how their data will be used
3. If the employee declines: document the refusal and keep on file. No further BEM obligation for this cycle.
4. If the employee accepts: schedule a BEM conversation including HR, the employee, their line manager (optional), and Works Council representative (if employee consents)
5. Identify causes of the absence (without requiring detailed medical information)
6. Agree and document measures: workplace adjustments, phased return, role modification, occupational health referral
7. Follow up on agreed measures and document progress
8. If illness continues and dismissal becomes necessary: Legal will rely on the completed BEM record to show the employer made genuine efforts

hr_authority.conditions: HR manages BEM. Escalate to Legal only if the BEM process reveals information that changes the employment situation (e.g., disability requiring Integrationsamt involvement) or if dismissal becomes the next step.

common_mistakes: Not offering BEM before an illness-related dismissal — courts regularly void such dismissals
Treating BEM as a box-ticking exercise with no genuine engagement
Pressuring the employee to disclose detailed medical information during BEM — this is not required and may be an AGG violation if disability-related

hr_scenarios.name: Employee Requests Reduction to Part-Time (Teilzeit)
hr_scenarios.description: An employee requests a reduction in working hours under the statutory part-time right.

notice_period.notes: No notice — this is a right to request, not a dismissal scenario.

hr_scenarios.works_council_note: Works Council co-determination on working time arrangements under § 87 Abs. 1 Nr. 2 BetrVG.
statutory_right_conditions: Employee has been employed for more than 6 months
The employer has more than 15 employees
Request must be made in writing at least 3 months before the desired start date
Employee must specify the desired working time and its distribution
employer_refusal_grounds: Examples: the reduced schedule cannot be covered, the role requires full-time presence for client or operational reasons
Refusal must be in writing and clearly justified — a vague 'operational need' is not sufficient
escalation_triggers: Employer wishes to refuse — Legal must assess whether the refusal grounds are sufficient
Employee is requesting part-time in connection with Elternzeit — different rules apply under BEEG § 15
The request would affect a team disproportionately and raises discrimination concerns
required_steps: 1. Acknowledge the request in writing within 1 month of receipt
2. Engage in good-faith discussions about the arrangement
3. If agreeing: document the new working time in a written amendment to the employment contract; involve Works Council
4. If refusing: assess whether compelling operational grounds exist — document in writing; if uncertain, escalate to Legal
5. Communicate the decision in writing before the start of the 1-month discussion window ends
6. Note: if the employer does not respond within 1 month, the employee's requested arrangement is deemed approved

hr_authority.conditions: Approval of part-time request. Escalate to Legal for refusals.

common_mistakes: Not responding within the 1-month window — silence equals approval
Refusing without adequate documented operational justification

hr_scenarios.name: Reference Letter (Arbeitszeugnis)
hr_scenarios.description: Employee requests a reference letter upon leaving — either a simple confirmation (einfaches Zeugnis) or a qualified reference (qualifiziertes Zeugnis).
employee_rights: Employee has a legal right to a Zeugnis upon request
Employee can request either a simple Zeugnis (dates and role) or a qualified Zeugnis (includes conduct and performance assessment)
The Zeugnis must be truthful but formulated benevolently (wohlwollend) — it must not prevent the employee from finding new work
Employee has the right to challenge a Zeugnis they believe is unfair at the Arbeitsgericht
hr_scenarios.coded_language_warning: German reference letters use a well-known coded language system. Seemingly positive phrases can carry negative meanings. Example: 'He tried his best' (Er war stets bemüht) = very poor performance. Agents should be aware of this when drafting.
escalation_triggers: Employee is challenging the content of a Zeugnis at the Arbeitsgericht
The honest assessment of the employee is very negative — Legal should review wording to ensure compliance with Wahrheitspflicht without creating unnecessary liability
required_steps: 1. Employee requests Zeugnis — note the type requested (simple or qualified)
2. Gather performance and conduct assessments from the line manager
3. Draft the Zeugnis using standard compliant language
4. Issue the Zeugnis promptly — unreasonable delay is a violation of the employer's obligation
5. Issue on company letterhead with wet-ink signature of an authorized representative

hr_authority.conditions: Standard Zeugnis drafting. Escalate to Legal if the employee challenges the content.
